purpose: Brimonidine eye drops are most commonly used to lower the pressure inside your eyes, which helps treat glaucoma and prevent damage to your vision. A separate eye drop version (Lumify) is used to reduce redness in your eyes. There is also a gel form (Mirvaso) used on the skin to reduce facial redness caused by rosacea.
how_it_works: Brimonidine works by stimulating certain receptors in your body that help reduce the amount of fluid your eye produces, while also helping more fluid drain out, which lowers the pressure in your eye. Think of it like opening a drain and reducing the water flowing in at the same time. In the skin gel form, it works by narrowing tiny blood vessels near the skin surface, which reduces the visible redness.
common_side_effects: Eye drops may cause mild stinging or burning when you put them in, eye redness, itching, dryness, blurred vision, or a feeling like something is in your eye. Some people feel drowsy or have a dry mouth. The skin gel may cause skin flushing or redness returning after it wears off.
warnings: Do not use brimonidine in children under 2 years old, as it can cause serious breathing problems and extreme sleepiness in young children. Tell your doctor if you take antidepressants called MAOIs, as this combination can be dangerous. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them. Let your doctor know if you have heart disease, low blood pressure, or kidney or liver problems.
typical_dosing: For glaucoma eye drops, the usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes about 3 times a day, roughly 8 hours apart. For the redness-relief eye drops (Lumify), use one drop in each eye every 6 to 8 hours as needed. For the facial redness gel (Mirvaso), a small pea-sized amount is applied to the face once daily. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions.
